answer: Map each identity by latency. Every epoch, a dozen randomly chosen verifiers on different continents send it signed pings, and the round-trip times form a fingerprint as distinct as a pigment in paint. Agents in separate datacenters show different mixes, while a farm of keys on one rack returns the same timings, like a meadow where every flower is one color. Identities whose fingerprints stay within 2 ms of each other for 10 epochs share one reward and one vote. A sybil can bridge that gap only by renting servers in new regions, so each fake costs real hosting.
